thread:
alan: Heads-up — after we shipped the Edge bundle built with esbuild, customers hit intermittent auth failures (401) only on production CDN builds. Local dev + unbundled works fine.

alan: Error in logs: `TypeError: headers.get is not a function` then downstream shows missing Authorization header. Happens when using the SDK as `import Redwood from 'redwood-sdk'` after bundling.

maya: Oof. Can you paste the minimal repro? which bundler + target? esbuild config?

alan: Using esbuild v0.19, target: "es2022", format: "esm", platform: "browser", bundle: true. Repro steps: `npm i && node ./scripts/run-edge-repro.js` -> fails only after `esbuild --bundle` output is deployed to edge worker.

alan: Package.json exports is non-trivial for us. snippet: ```json
{"name":"redwood-sdk","version":"2.1.0","exports": {"./package.json": "./package.json","./dist/cjs": {"require":"./dist/index.cjs.js"},".": {"import":"./dist/index.mjs","require":"./dist/index.cjs.js"}},"module":"dist/index.mjs","main":"dist/index.cjs.js"}```

nate: Hmm, interesting. If the default import ends up being `{ default: [Function] }` and edge runtime does `importScripts`/interop differently, the middleware that attaches Authorization header might be lost. Do you see the SDK's client factory function?

alan: When I log the imported value in bundle runtime I see `Object { default: undefined, createClient: [Function] }` (weird). In some bundles it becomes `default: [Function]` and `createClient: undefined` depending on minify + tree-shake.

jess: This screams conditional exports + bundler hoisting edge-case. Some bundlers prefer `module` field and rewrite ESM imports, others map through `exports`. Esbuild recently changed named export optimization for CJS->ESM interop.

ravi: Also check that the SDK does `export =` or `module.exports` compatibility. If the exported shape changed, a destructuring import like `import { createClient } from 'redwood-sdk'` could be undefined after bundling. That would lead to code that never sets auth header because the wrapper isn't invoked.

alan: Quick repro added: https://gist.github.com/alan/edge-esbuild-repro with two builds (esm vs cjs). Edge build (esm) strips the default and customer requests show no Authorization on the outgoing fetch.

maya: For immediate mitigation, try forcing the runtime import to the CJS entrypoint in esbuild: `alias: { 'redwood-sdk': path.resolve(__dirname, 'node_modules/redwood-sdk/dist/index.cjs.js') }` or set `conditions: ['node', 'default']`? Might be `conditions: ['browser']` causing an alternate path.

alan: Patch with alias -> Confirmed: pinned to cjs dist stops the auth drop. We saw 0 auth errors for the last 3 deploys.

jess: For fix upstream, we should publish a 2.1.1 that ensures the ESM entry uses named exports for all stable API surface, and add an `exports` fallback. Also add a note in README about bundlers + edge runtimes.

nate: Can we add a unit test that builds with esbuild and asserts the import shape before publish? Maybe a minimal smoke test in CI that runs esbuild and `node -e "import('file://...')..."`

security: Create an incident ticket and flag customer impact. support-bot: <https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/INC-7852|INC-7852> created, severity P2.

alan: I'll prepare a small patch and a reproducer PR. tagging @jess @nate for review. Thanks — I'll keep the thread updated. :thumbsup:

maya: Nice triage, team. Add changelog and a short migration note for customers using esbuild/turbopack.

alan: Last note — repro includes this quick log snippet that indicates header chain missing: ```
fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', { headers: req.headers })
// headers: { get: [Function: get], ... }  // good
// after bundle: { get: undefined, 'authorization': undefined } // bad
```

alan: Will push the PR by EOD and link here.
